Wish granted

One wish. Your whole delivery, granted.

The fastest way to deliver from Premiere Pro

One Click Export Pro turns exporting into configurable one-click buttons. Each button doesn't just render — it renames, verifies, packages, uploads, notifies and much more. Built for editors who deliver every day.

One panel

Everything in view, nothing buried

Sequences, source range, destination and naming — set once, then click a colored button to export. No digging through Adobe's dialogs.

  • Unlimited customizable export buttons
  • Premiere or Media Encoder, per button
  • Win & Mac, native on both

A pipeline behind every button

22 modules. One click.

Click any module to see how it worksTap any module to see how it works
Render engineRender with Premiere, or hand it to Media Encoder and keep editing while it exports in the background.
SequencesChoose what to export — all sequences, the active one, your selection, or a whole bin at once.
Source rangeExport the full timeline, just your In/Out, the work area, the section marked on the timeline, or the range of your selected clips.
Track soloExport with only the tracks you choose active — mute the extra cameras, language versions or music stems per button, and every track is put back afterwards.
DestinationDecide where each export lands — a set folder, the desktop, and more.
File nameName your files automatically — project, date, resolution and more — so they stay tidy and consistent.
WatermarkAdd a visible logo or text watermark on top of the exported video.
TimecodeBurn a running timecode onto the video — ideal for review copies, so clients can point to the exact moment in their notes.
MarkersTurn your timeline markers into chapters, or save them as a separate list.
MetadataWrite details like the title, author, copyright, file path and project name straight into the exported file.
ChecksumCreate a little verification file so you can be sure nothing got corrupted on the way to the client.
StillsGrab single frames from your video as image files — perfect for thumbnails, poster frames or a quick contact sheet.
InterchangeExport an AAF, FCP XML or OTIO of your timeline right next to the video — ready to hand off to Avid, DaVinci Resolve or another editing app.
TranscodeAutomatically make extra versions in other formats right after exporting — no second trip through Premiere.
CaptionsExport your subtitles and captions as separate files, ready to upload.
GraphicsExport a list of every on-screen title and graphic in your video — where each one sits and how long it runs.
PDF / CSVGet a clean delivery sheet listing everything you exported — handy to send with the files.
Annotate ProjectWrite delivery notes back into your Premiere project after exporting — bin columns and a colour label, so your project remembers what was sent.
DeliveryPack the export and its extras into one tidy delivery folder — with the option to zip it all up.
Cloud uploadSend your exports straight to Dropbox, Google Drive, OneDrive and more.
TelegramGet a Telegram message with a video preview, stills, a PDF and a download link, the moment your export is finished.
Run ScriptRun your own script after each export — copy to a NAS, notify another system, or kick off the next step. It runs as you, never as admin — use scripts you wrote or trust.

A few module features depend on upcoming Adobe Premiere Pro API updates and may not be available yet.

Auto-start Media Encoder queue
Only applies through Adobe Media Encoder. When ON, AME starts encoding immediately; when OFF, it queues the job for review.
Keep finished renders in Media Encoder
Only applies through Adobe Media Encoder. When ON, completed jobs stay in the queue as history.

Power features

Deliver & trigger anywhere

Upload to
DropboxSend finished exports straight to your Dropbox — pick the folder once and forget it.
DriveUpload exports to Google Drive automatically the moment they're done.
OneDrivePush your exports to OneDrive without ever leaving Premiere.
BoxDeliver exports to your Box account in a single click.
pCloudSend exports to pCloud as soon as they finish.

Smart file names

The names write themselves

Build every file name and folder path from live project data. Drop in tokens — project, sequence, date, codec, resolution — and OCEPro fills them in at export. Chain modifiers to pad, trim or re-case. No typing, no typos, no renaming.

{project}_{sequence}_{date}_{codec}
Acme_Promo_20260701_H264.mp4

File name

Project

{project}AcmeThe name of the project you’re in.
{sequence}PromoThe name of the sequence you’re exporting.
{bin}DeliverablesThe bin the sequence sits in.

{time}143020The time of day it went out.

{year}2026Just the four-digit year.

Clip & render

{preset}YouTube 4KThe export preset used.

{audioChannels}StereoMono, Stereo, 5.1 or Multichannel.

Frame size

{width}1920The width in pixels.
{height}1080The height in pixels.
{aspect}16x9The shape: 16x9, 9x16, 1x1.

Export frame

{timecode}01:00:04:12Where in the timeline you grabbed it.
{frame}512The frame number you grabbed.

Yours

{custom}you type itAsks you for a word when you click.
{button}MasterThe name of the button you clicked.
{space}blank spaceA real blank space.

Flags

{raw}keep ( ) [ ] !Keeps brackets and symbols.
{ascii}strip accentsRemoves the accents.

System folders

Folder-only

The difference

From 12 steps to 1 click

The old way

Twelve things — and you’re there for every one of them.

  1. Open the export dialog
  2. Pick the right preset
  3. Type the file name
  4. Choose the folder
  5. Start it and wait
  6. Find the file when it lands
  7. Make a checksum
  8. Write it into the delivery sheet
  9. Gather the stills and the report
  10. Zip the package
  11. Upload it and copy the link
  12. Write the delivery email

With One Click Export Pro

One click. Then you go back to editing.

Render H264

That’s the whole list — everything below runs on its own:

Renders & remuxesRenames from your tokensGenerates checksum + PDFPackages and zipsUploads to the cloudSends a Telegram with links

Getting started

Installing takes about a minute

Download the .ccx file from your aescripts account, then use whichever of these three you already have. Any of them does the same job.

Creative CloudYou already have Adobe’s Creative Cloud appZXP InstallerA free app from aescriptsaescripts managerTheir desktop app

Click any of the three for the exact steps. Once it is installed, the panel is in Premiere’s Window menu, under UXP Plugins.

If something doesn’t look right

Six things people run into. Find the one that sounds like what you are seeing.

“I installed it and Premiere doesn’t show it”Quit Premiere and open it again first: it only looks for new plugins when it starts. If it still is not there, your computer probably did not let the installer finish — see the last two answers.
“The panel opens but stays empty”Premiere uses a component from Adobe to draw the panel, and on some computers that component is old and never answers. It is not your files, your settings or your licence, and it is not something you can fix from the panel. Write to us and we will walk you through it.
“It says no compatible application was found”A warning that sounds worse than it is. aescripts’ own answer is to press Install anyway — it usually goes through. Make sure your installer is up to date first.
“It disappeared and I did not do anything”Opening an installer just to look at something can remove plugins you already had. Install it again, and from then on open the installer only when you actually mean to install something.
“The installer says it cannot install”Your computer is not letting programs be installed. Try the next answer first — it works without any special permissions. If that fails too, whoever looks after the computer has to run the installer.
“It is my work computer and I cannot install anything”The ZXP Installer can install just for you, with no administrator needed. Open its settings, tick “Install for current user only”, click OK, and install again. You can untick it afterwards.

Still stuck? Use the Help button at the top of this page — it writes the message for you. aescripts also keep a general FAQ that covers their installers. aescripts FAQ

HOW TO INSTALLCreative Cloud

The quickest one if the Creative Cloud app is already on your computer. Adobe’s own installer does the work.

Download the .ccx fileIt is in your aescripts account, under your orders.
Double-click itAdobe’s Creative Cloud installer opens and takes it from there.
Quit Premiere and open it againIt only looks for new plugins when it starts.
HOW TO INSTALLZXP Installer

Free, and it installs plugins for every Adobe application. aescripts say it also has a fallback for the cases where other installers — Adobe’s own included — fail.

Install the ZXP Installer onceFree, from aescripts. You only ever do this once.
Open it and add the .ccx fileOn a Mac, drag the file onto its window. On Windows, double-click the file.
Quit Premiere and open it againIt only looks for new plugins when it starts.

HOW TO INSTALLaescripts manager

Installs, licenses and updates everything you have bought from aescripts, in one click. Handy if you own more than one of their tools.

Install the aescripts + aeplugins appIt signs in with your aescripts account.
Find One Click Export Pro in your productsEverything you own is listed there.
Press Install, then restart PremiereThe app downloads and installs it for you.

If it will not start or log in, download it again: any copy from before October 2025 no longer works.

Before you buy

Very important things

The gaps in Adobe’s plugin API, in short. Better read now than found later.

Premiere Pro 26.3 or newerOn older versions the plugin will not load at all.
Keep the Work Area bar hiddenWhile it shows, Premiere ignores your In/Out points — in any export, not just ours. Work Area as a range is greyed out for the same reason.
H.265 / HEVC takes one extra stepThe API won’t write it directly. Add a Transcode module and it lands in the same click.
Text export: transcript onlyRun Speech to Text first. Captions can’t be read; graphics give titles and timings, not the words.
A few formats are Windows-onlyWindows Media and AVI have no encoder on macOS.
Interchange: AAF, XML, OTIOEDL, OMF and ALE are listed but don’t produce a file yet.
Project Manager is pausedVisible in the panel, but it does nothing for now.
Some codecs need Media EncoderOn the direct engine a few (DNxHR among them) write an empty file. One dropdown per button fixes it.
Three formats don’t export yetH.264 Blu-ray, P2 Movie and Wraptor DCP are listed but Adobe’s API doesn’t give the plugin an output file type for them.
This list keeps getting shorterEvery point waits on Adobe, not on us — we re-test each release and fix it in a free update. There’s a free trial: run your own formats before you spend anything.

Something not working?

Let’s get you unstuck

Most of what goes wrong has a one-minute fix. Start here — and if none of it helps, there is a right way to write to us.

I installed it but I can’t find the panel

In Premiere Pro open Window → UXP Plugins → One Click Export Pro. Premiere groups every UXP plugin under that one submenu, so it is not next to the older extensions.

If it is not in that list: the plugin needs Premiere Pro 26.3 or newer, and Premiere has to be restarted after installing it.

It says my licence is not activated

Open the panel menu — the ··· in the panel’s title bar — and choose About & License. You activate it there, with the licence from your aescripts account.

You need to be online the first time you activate. Buying and activating are two separate steps: a fresh install always asks once.

macOS: the panel opens but the licence never finishes checking

Almost always the same cause: macOS has flagged the downloaded files as quarantined, and the plugin cannot load the piece that checks your licence.

Download the plugin again from your aescripts account and let the aescripts manager install it. Do not copy an already-installed folder over from another Mac, and do not unzip it by hand — that is what carries the flag across.

The format I need is greyed out

Greyed out never means hidden: hover it and the panel tells you why. Either the format has no encoder on your operating system — Windows Media and AVI do not exist on macOS — or Adobe’s plugin API does not hand us an output file for it yet.

The full list of what is affected is in Very important things.

There is no H.265 / HEVC

Adobe’s plugin API refuses to write HEVC, in this plugin and in every other one — Premiere’s own export window is the only place it works.

The way around it is one click away: add a Transcode module to that button and the HEVC file lands in the same click as everything else.

I press the button and Media Encoder just sits there

That is Media Encoder waiting for you, not a failure. With Media Encoder as the engine the job is queued, and it only starts on its own if Auto-start Media Encoder queue is on in Settings.

So either press Play in Media Encoder, or turn that setting on and it will never wait again.

The file came out empty

A few codecs — DNxHR among them — write a zero-byte file when the export runs directly through Premiere.

Switch that button’s engine to Media Encoder. It is one dropdown, per button, and the same export writes a real file.

I changed too many settings and want to start over

Settings → Reset does not have to be all-or-nothing: it lists what it is about to reset by category — layout, buttons, stills, metadata — and you untick whatever you want to keep.

If you exported a settings backup before, restore that instead and you are exactly where you were.

If none of that helped

Write to us from inside the plugin

The panel attaches your Premiere Pro version, your operating system and your product version on its own. That is the difference between getting an answer and getting two emails asking which version you are on.

  1. Open the panel in Premiere Pro.Window → UXP Plugins → One Click Export Pro.
  2. Open the panel menu.The ··· in the panel’s title bar → About & License.
  3. Go to the Support tab and write it there.A subject, your email, and what happens. Your versions travel with it.

Please note: this page may contain inaccuracies, and parts of it may have been drafted with the help of AI, so some details could be wrong or out of date. That's exactly why a free trial is offered — try One Click Export Pro in your own setup before you buy. And because the plugin builds on Adobe's evolving UXP platform, a few capabilities shown here or visible in the panel may still depend on upcoming Adobe Premiere Pro API updates and may not be available yet.

MODULERender engine

Render with Premiere — or hand the export to Adobe Media Encoder and keep editing while it renders in the background.

Set it per button
Each export button can render with Premiere or Media Encoder — choose independently.
Keep editing
Media Encoder exports in the background while you keep working in Premiere.
Switch every button at once
Flip them all with the Engine control in the panel's top bar.
Lock the choice
Long-press the Engine control to force one engine for every button.
Stills and metadata probing still run briefly inside Premiere.
MODULESequences

Pick what each button exports — every sequence in the project, just the ones you selected, the one open on the timeline, or a whole bin at once.

All
Export every sequence in the project in one click.
Selected
Export only the sequences you selected in the Project panel.
Active
Export the sequence currently open on the timeline.
Bin
Drop sequences into a bin and export the whole bin together.
See what's matched
Right-click any option to list exactly which sequences it will export.
Lock it
Long-press so the panel always wins over a button's own setting.
MODULESource range

Export the whole timeline — or just your In/Out, the work area, a marked-up section, or the span of your selected clips.

Entire
Export the full sequence from start to end.
In-Out
Export only the section between your In and Out points.
Markers
Export between your in-color and out-color markers — click again to choose the colors.
Work Area
Greyed out for now — Adobe's API doesn't hand the work-area range to plugins.
Selection
Export the span covered by the clips you selected on the timeline.
Check the timecode
Right-click any option to see the start, end and duration before you export.
And keep the Work Area bar hidden while you work: while it shows, Premiere ignores your In/Out points in any export, not just ours.
MODULETrack solo

Export a version with only the tracks you want — mute the extra cameras, language versions or music stems per button, and get clean cuts without ever touching your timeline.

Solo your video tracks
Keep every video track, pick them by number, or match them by name — the rest are muted just for this export.
Solo your audio tracks
Do the same for audio — isolate a language, a music stem or a clean mix, chosen live from the active sequence.
One cut, or one per track
Export a single version with just the active tracks, or a separate file for each soloed track in one go.
Puts everything back
Your tracks' mute states are restored the moment the export finishes — even if you cancel midway.
If nothing matches your track-name filter, the export safely falls back to all tracks — so you never end up with a silent or empty file by accident.
MODULEDestination

Decide where each export lands — a folder you set, a folder it asks for every time, the Desktop, or straight to the cloud.

Set a folder
Point a button at a fixed folder, with subfolders built from path tokens like {project} and {date}.
Ask each time
Have it ask you for the destination folder right before every export.
Desktop
Send the export straight to your Desktop with one click.
Cloud
Export directly to Dropbox, Google Drive, OneDrive, Box, pCloud or your own server.
Open the folder
Alt-click any destination to open that folder on your computer.
Lock it
Long-press so the destination always wins over a button's own setting.
How path tokens work
MODULEFile name

Name your exported files automatically — after the sequence, by asking you each time, or from a reusable template of project, date, resolution and more.

Sequence
Name each file after its sequence, so the export matches the timeline.
Ask each time
Have it ask you for the file name before every export.
Template
Build names from tokens like {project}, {date} and {aspect} — click again to edit.
Reusable templates
Keep several named templates and switch between them per button.
Preview the name
Turn on a live preview to see the finished file name before you export.
Lock it
Long-press so the naming always wins over a button's own setting.
How tokens work
MODULEWatermark

Stamp a logo image or a line of text on top of your exported video — pick the spot, size and how see-through it is.

Logo or text
Drop in a logo image, or type text in your choice of font and colour.
Place it anywhere
Nine positions — corners, edges or dead-center — with a margin and opacity you control.
Size it
Scale the logo to a share of the frame width, or set the text size.
Keep the clean one
Leave the original untouched and get a separate watermarked copy instead.
Because the mark is baked into the picture, the video is re-rendered into a fresh file — so this export takes a bit longer.
MODULETimecode

Burn a running timecode onto the picture — perfect for review copies, so clients can point to the exact moment in their notes.

Choose the count
Run it from the sequence, the source clip, zero, or a custom start — as timecode, frame number or seconds.
Place and style it
Nine positions, your size, font, colour, opacity and an optional background box.
Add a label
Put a label like the sequence name or date beside the timecode.
Up to four lines
Save up to four timecode lines and burn them all at once — they auto-stack so they don't overlap.
Keep the clean one
Leave the master untouched and get a separate copy with the timecode.
Baked into the picture, so the video is re-rendered into a new file. "Source clip" mode skips any clip that was sped up or reversed.
MODULEMarkers

Turn your timeline markers into chapter lists — ready for YouTube, a spreadsheet, or to hand to another editor.

Pick your markers
Filter by marker type — Chapter, Comment, Web link, Flash — and by colour.
Choose the format
Export a YouTube chapter list, a spreadsheet, a structured list, or an Avid marker list — any combination.
Saved beside the video
Each list is written as its own file right next to the exported video.
Link back after upload
After a cloud upload, drop a marker on your timeline holding the share link.
Premiere's default markers are the "Comment" type, not "Chapter" — tick Comment too, or you may get an empty list.
MODULEMetadata

Write details like the title, author, copyright, project name and file path straight into the exported file.

Auto details
Fills in title, author, project, sequence, resolution, date and more from the export itself.
Your own fields
Add any custom label-and-value pairs, filled in from project, date or filename for you.
Inside the file or beside it
Embed the details into the file, and/or save a companion details file next to it.
Some formats — like MXF, ProRes-MXF, DPX, OpenEXR and Windows Media — can't store details inside, so a companion file is saved alongside instead.
MODULEChecksum

Create a tiny verification file alongside each export, so the client can confirm the file arrived without a single byte changing.

Pick the check type
Choose the verification strength, or create several at once.
One file per export
Each finished file gets its own small verification file right next to it.
Everywhere or per button
A global switch forces it on for every export, leaves it to each button, or turns it off.
MODULEStills

Grab single frames from your timeline as image files — great for thumbnails, poster frames or a quick contact sheet.

Pick an image format
Export as JPG, PNG, TIFF, OpenEXR, DPX, Targa, BMP or GIF, with per-format options.
Set the size
Keep full resolution or drop to half or quarter.
Choose which frames
Grab the playhead, first or last frame, your In or Out, every clip cut, or markers of a colour.
Or grab on a schedule
Pull a frame every few frames or seconds for an instant contact sheet.
BMP and GIF only work on Windows — on Mac, Premiere can't write those two.
MODULEInterchange

Export an AAF, FCP-XML or OTIO of your timeline right next to the video, ready to hand off to Avid, DaVinci Resolve or another editing app.

Pick the format
Choose AAF, FCP-XML or OTIO — the formats other editing apps can open.
Fine-tune AAF
For AAF, set audio handling, sample rate, source trimming and handles.
Name it and place it
Give the file its own name and folder, or let it sit beside the video.
This writes a timeline file, so the button needs a sequence. Moving the whole project for archiving is a separate feature, not part of this.
MODULETranscode

Automatically make extra versions in other formats the moment your master finishes — no second trip through Premiere.

Add as many versions
Queue several extra outputs, each with its own format preset.
Name and sort each
Give every version a suffix and its own folder, and tag it with a role like web or social.
Verify each version
Optionally create a verification file for each extra version.
Skip the paused ones
Turn any version on or off without deleting its setup.
Each extra version is a full render, so more versions means more time after the main export.
MODULECaptions

Export your subtitles and captions as separate files — ready to upload alongside the video or hand to a captioning house.

Pick the source
Today it's the Speech to Text transcript. Reading your caption tracks is still waiting on Adobe.
Web subtitle files
Tick the everyday subtitle formats for web and review.
Broadcast formats
Need broadcast-ready files? Turn them on too.
One file per track
Keep each language or caption track in its own file.
Text encoding
Choose the encoding so accents and non-Latin scripts come out clean.
Reading caption text is waiting on an upcoming Premiere Pro update, so this module sits greyed out in the panel for now.
MODULEGraphics

Get a tidy list of every on-screen title and graphic used in your timeline — exported next to the video as a spreadsheet or simple text file.

Choose what to scan
Just the graphic-style clips, only the top track, or every track.
Spreadsheet or text
Save the list as a spreadsheet, a structured file, or plain text.
Text encoding
Pick the encoding so titles in any language read correctly.
Skip the blanks
Leave out empty entries so the list stays clean.
Reading the actual title text is waiting on an upcoming Premiere Pro update — for now you get where titles sit, not the words themselves.
MODULEPDF / CSV

Generate a clean delivery sheet listing everything you just exported — pick a polished PDF, a running spreadsheet, or both.

PDF delivery sheet
A polished page listing every file with its format, resolution, duration and size.
Checksum QR code
Add a scannable code so the client can confirm the file arrived intact.
Running file list
Keep a cumulative spreadsheet that adds a row every time you deliver.
Include your markers
Add your timeline markers to the PDF as a delivery note.
Your studio logo
Drop in a logo and choose the sheet's language to match your brand.
MODULEAnnotate Project

Write delivery notes straight back onto your Premiere project after exporting — so your bins remember what was sent and when.

Fill in bin columns
Auto-write the Description, Comment or Log Note columns using tokens.
Stamp as delivered
Tag the clip with a hidden "delivered" note carrying the date and destination.
Set a colour label
Recolour the bin item after delivery so finished work stands out.
Choose the target
Apply it to the active sequence's bin item, your selected clips, or both.
This one changes your Premiere project — it edits columns, labels and notes on your bins. Save first to be safe.
MODULEDelivery

Pack the export and all its extras — the master, transcodes, checksums, PDF — into one tidy, client-ready folder, with an option to zip it all up.

Choose the layout
A clean structure, a flat folder, or your own folder template.
Name the folder
Build the folder name from project, sequence, date and a client reference.
Add a manifest
Drop in a contents list that can also record each file's checksum.
Zip it up
Bundle everything into a single zip, ready to hand off.
Split huge zips
Break a very large zip into numbered parts, each with its own checksum.
Verify the zip
Check the finished zip opens cleanly before you send it.
Turn on 'delete folder after zip' and only the zip is kept — the loose folder is removed.
MODULECloud upload

Send finished exports straight to Dropbox, Google Drive, OneDrive, Box, pCloud or your own FTP/SFTP server — and get a ready-to-share link back automatically.

Pick your service
Dropbox, Google Drive, OneDrive, Box, pCloud, or FTP / SFTP.
Authenticate once
Sign in through your browser, paste an access token, or enter your FTP details — kept in the plugin's encrypted storage, never in the settings file.
Set the folder
Point it at a destination folder, using tokens like project and date.
Choose what goes up
Send the zip, every file, or let it pick automatically when Delivery is on.
Get a share link
A shareable link is created automatically and can be reused in your Telegram message.
You need a connected account and an internet connection. Very large files are sent up in pieces automatically.
MODULETelegram

The moment an export finishes, get a Telegram message with a short video preview, the still frames, the delivery PDF and your download links.

Set it up once
Save your bot once, then add the chats it should message — a Detect button finds them.
Attach the extras
Optionally include the still frames, the delivery PDF, and your download links.
Send a preview
Attach a short clip — the whole video, or just the first or last few seconds.
Pick the language
Write the message in any of the plugin's languages, or match your panel.
Test it
Fire off a test message to make sure it lands before your next export.
You need a Telegram bot and a chat set up first. The video preview must stay small, so longer clips are trimmed or skipped.
How to set it up
MODULERun Script

Run your own script after each export — copy the file to a NAS, ping another system, or kick off the next step. It runs as you, never as an administrator.

Pick your script
Choose a script from the managed folder; ready-made examples are waiting inside.
Get the details
Hand your script the file path, name, sequence, project and format, automatically.
Run free or wait
Let it run in the background, or wait with a safety time limit so an export never hangs.
Test it
Run the script on demand to check it works before wiring it to a button.
Scripts run with your own permissions — never as an administrator — and live in one managed folder, so an imported setup can't point at a stranger's script.
SETUP GUIDESet up your Telegram bot

A one-time setup, about two minutes — create a bot, paste its token, and point it at your chat.

1
Create your bot
In Telegram, message @BotFather, send /newbot and pick a name — he replies with your bot token.
2
Paste the token
Copy that token into the module's Bot token field. Keep it private — it controls your bot.
3
Message your bot
Search your new bot in Telegram and send it anything, so it's allowed to write to you.
4
Add the chat
Hit Detect to find the chat automatically — or paste a chat ID from @userinfobot.
5
Send a test
Press Test to confirm the message arrives. Every export now pings Telegram.
Your bot token is kept in the plugin's encrypted storage — never in the settings file.
Back to what it does
UPLOADDropbox

Send finished exports straight to your Dropbox — pick the folder once and forget it.

Connect once
Sign in to Dropbox in your browser — it shows a short access code.
Paste the code
Copy that code into the plugin's Authorization code field to finish connecting.
Pick a folder
Choose where uploads land, building the path from project, date and more.
On first connect Dropbox may flag it as a 'small app' — that's expected, it's our own connector. Your login stays in the plugin's encrypted storage.
UPLOADDrive

Upload exports to Google Drive automatically the moment they're done.

Connect once
Sign in to Google in your browser — the plugin usually connects on its own.
Or paste the code
If it doesn't connect automatically, copy the Authorization code into the plugin.
Point at a folder
Right-click a Drive folder → Get link, and paste the share URL (or its folder ID).
UPLOADOneDrive

Push your exports to OneDrive without ever leaving Premiere.

Connect once
Sign in to Microsoft in your browser — the plugin picks it up automatically.
Or paste the code
If it doesn't auto-connect, copy the Authorization code into the plugin.
Set the folder
Choose the destination folder for your uploads.
UPLOADBox

Deliver exports to your Box account in a single click.

Connect once
Sign in to Box in your browser; it returns to the plugin automatically.
Or paste the code
If needed, copy the Authorization code into the plugin.
Set the folder
Choose where uploads land.
Box charges for its Platform API calls, so heavy uploading may count against your Box plan.
UPLOADpCloud

Send exports to pCloud as soon as they finish.

Connect once
Sign in to pCloud — it shows an access code and a server hostname.
Paste the code
Enter the code into the plugin to connect.
Set the folder
Choose the destination folder.
The pCloud code expires after about ten minutes, so paste it promptly.
UPLOADFTP / SFTP

Upload straight to your own server over FTP — or secure SFTP.

Enter the server
Fill in Host, Port, Username and Password, plus a Remote Path for the uploads.
Go secure
Flip 'Use SFTP' for an encrypted transfer.
Test it
Hit Test Connection to confirm it works before you rely on it.
Your password is kept in the plugin's encrypted storage — never in the settings file.
UPLOADTelegram

When an export finishes, a Telegram message lands with everything your client needs — at a glance.

Instant ping
A message arrives the moment the export is done — headed 'Export complete' with the date and time.
Files attached
The delivery PDF and still frames come attached, plus a short video preview when it fits Telegram's size limit.
Share links
Every uploaded file gets a public download link, listed per cloud — your client just clicks and grabs it.
Owner folders
Links to the folders in each of your own clouds are included too (those ask for your sign-in).
UPLOADShare link

Get a ready-to-share public link for every file you upload — the person you send it to needs no account.

One link per file
Each uploaded file (the master, the PDF, the stills…) comes back with its own public download link.
No sign-in for them
Anyone with the link downloads it directly — no Dropbox or Drive account required.
Reused everywhere
The same links appear in your Telegram message and the delivery report.
TRIGGERMIDI

Fire an export by pressing a pad or key on a MIDI controller — Loupedeck, Akai, Korg and more.

Map a pad
Assign any export button to a pad or key on your controller.
One press = export
Hit the pad and the export runs — your hands stay off the keyboard.
TRIGGERHTTP

Start an export from another app or device — like a Stream Deck — over your network.

A simple web call
Any device on your network can trigger an export with a small web request.
Locked to you
A secret token keeps it private — only requests carrying the token fire an export.
TRIGGERHotkey

Launch an export with a keyboard shortcut — hands stay on the keyboard.

Assign a shortcut
Bind any export button to a key combination.
Tap to export
Press it and the export runs instantly.
EXPORT TYPEMedia

The everyday export: your sequence rendered out as a video or audio file — with the whole module pipeline running behind the click.

Any format Premiere can export
ProRes, H.264, DNxHR and DNxHD, MXF, QuickTime, MPEG-2 and more — plus audio-only WAV, AIFF, MP3 or AAC.
Your own presets too
Use Premiere's built-in presets, or drop the ones you saved yourself into the plugin's preset folder and pick them like any other.
One button per delivery
Build a button for every format you hand over — each with its own colour, name, destination, naming and pipeline.
H.265 / HEVC — through Transcode
Adobe doesn't let plugins export HEVC directly. Set the button to ProRes or DNxHR and add a Transcode module set to H.265: same one click, HEVC at the end.
That HEVC block is Adobe's, not ours — Premiere's own Export window still writes it by hand. Leave H.265 as a button's main format and the export will simply report it can't run.
EXPORT TYPEStill

Pull single frames straight out of your timeline as image files — poster frames, thumbnails, review stills or a whole contact sheet.

Pick the image format
JPG, PNG, TIFF, OpenEXR, DPX, Targa, BMP or GIF, each with its own quality options.
Choose which frames
The playhead, the first or last frame, your In or Out points, every clip cut, or markers of a colour you choose.
Or grab on a schedule
Take a frame every few frames or every few seconds and get an instant contact sheet.
Set the size
Keep full resolution, or drop to half or quarter.
BMP and GIF are Windows-only — on Mac, Premiere can't write those two.
EXPORT TYPEProject data

Hand your timeline over to another editing app — an AAF for Avid, an FCP-XML for DaVinci Resolve or Final Cut, an OTIO for everything else.

AAF, FCP-XML, OTIO
The three formats other editing apps can actually open, written straight from your sequence.
Fine-tune the AAF
Set audio handling, sample rate, source trimming and handles before it's written.
Several files, one click
A button can hold more than one output — hand off an AAF and an XML together.
Or ship it with the video
Prefer it beside the master? The Interchange module adds the same file to any Media button's export.
EDL, OMF and Avid Log (ALE) buttons are there for completeness, but Premiere's plugin API still has no exporter for them — they're waiting on an Adobe update.
EXPORT TYPEProxy

Turn the footage in your timeline into lightweight proxies and attach them to your project — one click, no trip through Media Encoder.

Reads your timeline
It walks the sequence, finds every unique video clip and works from the original media.
Pick the proxy flavour
ProRes Proxy, H.264 QuickTime or MP4, CineForm, or the VR variants — at full, half, quarter or a size you set.
Attached automatically
Finished proxies are linked back to their clips, so you can switch to them the moment it's done.
Skip or rebuild
Leave already-proxied clips alone, or force the whole batch to be regenerated after you change size or format.
Optional watermark
Stamp a logo or text on the proxies only — handy for review copies that must never pass as the master.
Proxies are built from the original media files, so the footage has to be online. Anything Premiere can't proxy is skipped and reported at the end.
EXPORT TYPEText

Get your timeline's text out as separate files — the Speech to Text transcript today, with caption tracks and on-screen titles waiting on Adobe.

Transcript
Takes Premiere's Speech-to-Text transcript and writes it out as subtitle files or plain text.
Readable subtitles, optional
Instead of Adobe's one-long-cue-per-sentence output, re-cut the transcript into proper subtitles — line length and reading speed following the usual broadcast standards.
Captions
Reads your caption tracks and saves them as web or broadcast subtitle files — one file per track if you prefer.
Graphics
Scans your titles and Essential Graphics and lists them as a spreadsheet, a structured file or plain text.
Encoding & separators
Choose the text encoding and the spreadsheet separator so accents and non-Latin scripts come out clean.
Transcript exports work today. Reading caption-track and on-screen title text is still waiting on an upcoming Premiere Pro update, so those two may come out empty for now.
SETUPA workspace per client

A workspace is the whole panel saved under a name: buttons, destinations, naming, modules, layout. Switch from the top bar and everything follows.

As many as you need
One per client, per format, per team — each with its own colour dot so you know at a glance where you are.
Start from anything
Create a workspace empty, or duplicate the one you already trust and tweak it.
Switching is instant
Mid-export it waits politely: the switch happens the moment the render is done, never in the middle.
PER BUTTONOne button, many renders

Give a button several profiles and one click runs them in order — the master, the review copy and the social crop, from a single press.

Each profile is complete
Its own format, name, destination and modules. They are not variations of one export; they are separate exports.
Turn them on and off
Keep a profile in the button but leave it disabled until the day you need it again.
Different places at once
Master to the NAS, review copy to Dropbox, vertical crop to the client folder — same click.
LAYOUTHide what you never use

Every section and option of the panel can be turned off, so what is left is only what you actually use.

Sections or single options
Hide a whole block — Project data, Proxy, Text — or just the options inside one you never pick.
Nothing is lost
A hidden option keeps its settings. Turn it back on months later and it is exactly as you left it.
The grid follows
Fewer sections means a shorter panel, which matters when it lives in a docked column.
FITS YOUR SCREENPanel size

The panel goes from a narrow strip docked beside the timeline to a wide window on a second monitor, and the whole interface scales with it.

Any width
Set a minimum and a maximum, or let it fill whatever space you give it.
Interface scale
Make everything bigger or smaller independently of the width — useful on 4K laptops and on studio displays alike.
LAYOUTButton grid

Choose how many export buttons sit side by side, per section — a wide grid of small buttons, or a short column of big ones.

Per section
Media, Stills, Project data, Proxy and Text each keep their own column count.
Reorder freely
Drag a button where it belongs; the ones you press every day go first.
AT A GLANCEButton colours

Colour is how you find the right button without reading it. Pick from the palette or type your own value.

Your own colours
Thirteen ready-made fills, plus any colour you like — the ones you type are kept for next time.
Label colour too
Set the text colour per button when a fill needs a lighter or darker label than the default.
FILE NAMESName templates

Save the naming patterns you use as templates and point each button at the one it needs.

Several at once
Keep a template for masters, one for review copies, one for the client's own convention.
Named, not numbered
Give each one a name you recognise, then switch a button from one to another in a click.
INTERFACE23 languages

The whole panel — labels, tooltips, messages and reports — speaks your language. Switch at any time from Settings; nothing else changes.

Latin alphabet
Bahasa Melayu · Català · Dansk · Deutsch · English · Español · Français · Italiano · Nederlands · Norsk · Polski · Português · Svenska · Tiếng Việt · Türkçe
Cyrillic
Русский · Українська
Asian scripts
हिन्दी · 中文 · 日本語 · 한국어
Right to left
العربية · עברית — the whole interface mirrors, not just the text.
YOUR SETUPBackup & restore

Your whole configuration is a file you own — take it to another machine, or roll back to how things were.

Move it anywhere
Back up on one computer, import on the next, and your panel is the same as the one you left.
Reset what you choose
Put one area back to factory — buttons, destinations, triggers — without touching the rest. Your own presets are always kept.
NAMING TOKEN{project}

The name of the Premiere project you have open. When several jobs land in the same folder — or on the same server — this is what tells them apart, and it follows the day you rename the project.

{project}_{sequence}Acme_Promo
{project}_{date}Acme_20260701
NAMING TOKEN{sequence}

The name of the sequence being exported, and the usual backbone of a file name. Its real value shows when one click covers ten sequences: each file comes out named after its own, with no typing and no chance of a mismatch.

{sequence}_{date}Promo_20260701
{sequence}_{codec}Promo_H264
NAMING TOKEN{bin}

The bin your sequence lives in. If you already organise the project by client, by deliverable or by version, that organisation carries into the file name on its own — you never have to repeat it by hand.

{bin}_{sequence}Deliverables_Promo
NAMING TOKEN{date}

The day of the export, which sorts chronologically on its own in any file browser. It takes whatever format you ask for — ISO, European, short — so it can match a client’s naming spec instead of fighting it.

{sequence}_{date}Promo_20260701
{sequence}_{date:DD-MM-YYYY}Promo_01-07-2026
NAMING TOKEN{time}

The time of day the export ran. It’s what tells apart two versions that went out the same afternoon, when the date alone would give them the same name.

{sequence}_{time}Promo_143020
NAMING TOKEN{timestamp}

Date and time in one go. The simplest way to never overwrite yesterday’s render — or this morning’s: every click produces a name that has never existed before.

{sequence}_{timestamp}Promo_20260701-143020
NAMING TOKEN{year}

Just the year. Common in broadcast and marketing naming, where the campaign year is part of the deliverable’s identity and the rest of the date is noise.

{sequence}_{year}Promo_2026
NAMING TOKEN{codec}

The format the file was written in. When the same cut goes out as ProRes for the grade and H.264 for review, the name says which is which — so nobody opens the wrong one.

{sequence}_{codec}Promo_H264
NAMING TOKEN{preset}

The name of the export preset. More precise than the format alone: it tells YouTube 4K from YouTube 1080p, or your own saved preset from Adobe’s, and it follows if you point the button at a different one.

{sequence}_{preset}Promo_YouTube 4K
NAMING TOKEN{framerate}

Frames per second of the sequence. Some clients want it in the name and some archives require it — either way, reading it from the sequence means you never type the wrong one.

{sequence}_{framerate}fpsPromo_25fps
NAMING TOKEN{duration}

How long the exported piece runs, in whole seconds. Made for spots and cutdowns, where the length is part of the name — and it follows your In and Out points, so a 30-second version really says 30.

{sequence}_{duration}sPromo_30s
NAMING TOKEN{audioChannels}

The audio layout of the sequence — Mono, Stereo, 5.1 or Multichannel. Worth having in the name whenever the same picture ships with two different mixes.

{sequence}_{audioChannels}Promo_Stereo
NAMING TOKEN{frames}

How many frames went out. Useful for image sequences, and for checking at a glance that a conform came back the same length it left at.

{sequence}_{frames}fPromo_750f
NAMING TOKEN{width}

The width of the picture in pixels. Usually paired with the height for a plain, readable size that any client understands without a spec sheet.

{sequence}_{width}x{height}Promo_1920x1080
NAMING TOKEN{height}

The height of the picture in pixels. Usually paired with the width for a plain, readable size that any client understands without a spec sheet.

{sequence}_{width}x{height}Promo_1920x1080
NAMING TOKEN{aspect}

The shape of the picture: 16x9, 9x16, 1x1. The token that saves you when one cut goes out in three crops for social — each file names its own shape, so nothing gets posted sideways.

{sequence}_{aspect}Promo_16x9
{sequence}_{aspect:decimal}Promo_1.78
NAMING TOKEN{timecode}

The timecode of the frame you grabbed, so months later you can jump straight back to that exact spot in the timeline instead of hunting for it.

{sequence}_TC{timecode}Promo_TC01-00-04-12
File names can’t hold colons, so they come out as dashes.
NAMING TOKEN{frame}

The frame number you grabbed. Pad it out and a folder full of stills finally sorts in the right order, instead of putting frame 1000 before frame 9.

{sequence}_F{frame}Promo_F512
{sequence}_F{frame-pad(6)}Promo_F000512
NAMING TOKEN{custom}

Asks you for a word the moment you click, and drops it into the name. For the one thing that changes every time and no project data can know — a version, a client, a note to yourself.

{custom}_{sequence}_{date}Client_Promo_20260701
NAMING TOKEN{button}

The name of the button you clicked. One button called Master and another called Social, and every file says where it came from — without configuring two naming patterns.

{button}_{sequence}Master_Promo
NAMING TOKEN{space}

A real blank space. Names are tidied up by default — runs of spaces collapse, edges get trimmed — so this is how you ask for one on purpose and keep it.

{sequence}{space}{date}Promo 20260701
NAMING TOKEN{raw}

Keeps the characters that would otherwise be cleaned out of a name — brackets, parentheses, exclamation marks. Drop it anywhere in the pattern and it covers the whole name, not just the token next to it.

{sequence} (final){raw}Promo (final)
NAMING TOKEN{ascii}

Strips the accents from everything the pattern produces, so a name travels safely to servers, FTPs and clients that only speak plain letters. Like {raw}, it applies to the whole name wherever you put it.

Sequence “Épisode” + {ascii}Episode
PATH TOKEN{projectpath}

The folder your project file lives in. Everything you export stays next to the project — move the project to another drive and the exports follow, because the path is worked out at export time.

{projectpath}/Exports…/Acme/Exports
{projectpath}/Exports/{date}…/Acme/Exports/20260701
PATH TOKEN{desktop}

Your Desktop. For the export you want to see the second it lands, without going looking for it.

{desktop}/ExportsDesktop/Exports
PATH TOKEN{documents}

Your Documents folder — the usual home for the paperwork that travels with a delivery: reports, checksums, packages.

{documents}/ExportsDocuments/Exports
PATH TOKEN{downloads}

Your Downloads folder. Useful as a scratch destination for things that are only passing through on their way somewhere else.

{downloads}/ExportsDownloads/Exports
PATH TOKEN{videos}

Your videos folder — Movies on a Mac, Videos on Windows. One pattern, and it lands in the right place on either machine without a second setup.

{videos}/{project}Movies/Acme
PATH TOKEN{movies}

The same folder as {videos}, under the name a Mac user expects to see. Both tokens resolve to the same place on both systems, so pick whichever reads better to you.

{movies}/{project}Movies/Acme
PATH TOKEN{pictures}

Your Pictures folder — where a batch of stills usually belongs, and where the rest of your photo tools will go looking for them.

{pictures}/{sequence}Pictures/Promo
PATH TOKEN{music}

Your Music folder, for the audio-only exports: a WAV mix to hand over, an MP3 for approval.

{music}/{project}Music/Acme
PATH TOKEN{home}

Your user folder — the one that holds Desktop, Documents and the rest. The starting point when you want to build a path of your own.

{home}/RendersHome/Renders
PATH TOKEN{oce}

The plugin’s own folder inside Documents, where its reports, packages and temporary files already live. Keeps everything the plugin makes in one place.

{oce}/{project}OneClickExportPRO/Acme
PATH TOKEN{production}

A name you set once for the job — the client, the campaign, the season — and every path can use. Change it when the job changes and every button follows.

{desktop}/{production}/{sequence}Desktop/Acme 2026/Promo
PATH TOKEN{role}

What the export is for: master, web, social. Lets a single click drop each version in its own folder, without a separate destination per button.

{projectpath}/Exports/{role}…/Acme/Exports/Master
PATH TOKEN{separator}

The slash your system uses — / on a Mac, \ on Windows. Only needed when you build a path piece by piece and want it right on both machines.

{projectpath}{separator}Exports…/Acme/Exports
PANELSequences

Choose which sequences this button exports — all of them, the ones you selected, the active one, or your _OneClickExport bin.

All
Click to export every sequence in the project.
Selected
Click to export only the sequences you've selected.
Active
Click to export the sequence open in the timeline.
Bin
Click to export everything inside the _OneClickExport bin.
Lock it
Long-press a mode so it always wins over a button's own setting.
See what's matched
Right-click to list the sequences this button would export.
PANELSource range

Pick how much of the sequence goes out — the whole thing, your In/Out, between markers, the work area, or just a selection.

Entire
Click to export the whole sequence from start to end.
In / Out
Click to export only between your In and Out points.
Markers
Click to export between markers — click again to set the In/Out colours.
Work Area
Click to export the highlighted work-area bar.
Selection
Click to export just the clips selected on the timeline.
Lock it
Long-press so this range always wins over a button's own setting.
Timecode info
Right-click to read the In/Out and duration of the chosen range.
PANELDestination

Choose where the file lands — a fixed folder, by asking you each time, the Desktop, or a connected cloud.

Path
Click to always save to a folder you set.
Ask

PANELOverwrite

Decide what happens when a file with the same name already exists where you're exporting.

Replace
When it's on, a new export overwrites a file that already has the same name.
Keep both

Name it uniquely
Add {timestamp} or {custom} to your file name to avoid clashes in the first place.
PANEL · TOKENSFile name tokens

A template turns tokens — little {placeholders} — into a real file name at export time. Mix them with your own text, then fine-tune with modifiers. Here's every token and exactly what it becomes.

Project
{project}your project's name — Acme_Promo
{sequence}the sequence's name — Main_v3
{bin}the bin the sequence sits in — Deliverables (ROOT if it's at the top)
Date & time
{date}the day — 20260619
{time}the time — 143052
{timestamp}day + time, unique per export — 20260619-143052
{year}2026
{date:YYYY-MM-DD}your own layout — 2026-06-19. Works on {date}, {time} and {timestamp}; the pieces are YYYY YY MM DD HH mm SS, so {time:HH-mm} → 14-30
Format & size
{width}1920
{height}1080
{aspect}smart aspect — 16x9 (or 2.39 for cinema)
{aspect:ratio}always width×height — 16x9
{aspect:decimal}always a decimal — 1.78
{framerate}frames per second — 25
{duration}length of the export in seconds — 90
{audioChannels}Stereo, 5.1, Mono…
{codec}the codec preset — ProRes 422
{preset}the export preset's name
This export
{button}the button you clicked — Render H264
{custom}pops up and asks you for text just before exporting
{space}a real space (templates trim loose spaces, so use this for a deliberate one)
Still frames only
{frame}the grabbed frame's number — 42
{timecode}that frame's timecode — 00-01-30-12
{frames}total number of frames
Modifiers — reshape any token
{sequence-upper}MAIN_V3 · -lower → main_v3 · -cap → Main_v3
{frame-pad(5)}pad with leading zeros — 00042
{sequence-left(4)}first N characters — Main · -right(4) → the last N
{sequence-replace(_,-)}swap one piece for another — Main-v3
Chaining & rules
Chain modifiers: {sequence-upper-left(8)}. One rule — you can't mix a :format and a -modifier on the same token.
Keeping names clean
These are stripped from names automatically: / \ : * ? " < > | and more. Add {raw} anywhere to keep punctuation like ( ) [ ] !; add {ascii} to flatten accents (café → cafe).
You type{project}_{sequence-upper}_{date}
You getAcme_Promo_MAIN-V3_20260619
You type{sequence}{space}{aspect}{space}{timestamp}
You getMain_v3 16x9 20260619-143052
Back to File name
PANEL · TOKENSPath tokens

A destination folder is built in two passes: first a root token picks which folder on the computer to start in, then folder tokens add subfolders from your project, date and more.

Start here — root folder (pass 1)
{oce}~/Documents/OneClickExportPRO
{projectpath}the folder your .prproj lives in
{desktop}~/Desktop
{documents}~/Documents
{downloads}~/Downloads
{movies}your movies folder — ~/Movies on Mac, ~/Videos on Windows ({videos} is the same)
{pictures}~/Pictures
{music}~/Music
{home}your user folder
Then subfolders — per export (pass 2)
{project}Acme_Promo
{sequence}Main_v3
{bin}the sequence's bin
{date}20260619 · {year} → 2026
{production}your Premiere Production name (empty on a standalone project)
{codec}ProRes 422 · {button} → the button's name
{role}Master / Proxy / Web… (when Delivery Package is on)
{width} {height} {framerate}1920 · 1080 · 25
{separator}your OS folder separator · {space} → a literal space
How it resolves
Pass 1 swaps the root token for a real folder, then pass 2 fills the subfolder tokens. Slashes and backslashes are made native to your OS automatically, and {projectpath} needs an open project. The same modifiers and date formats as file names work here too — e.g. {project-upper}, {date:YYYY-MM}.
You type{oce}/{project}/{date}
You get/Users/you/Documents/OneClickExportPRO/Acme_Promo/20260619
You type{desktop}/{project-upper}_{role}
You get/Users/you/Desktop/ACME_PROMO_Master
Back to Destination

SETTINGSWhen a file already exists

An export that would write over a file you already have asks you first — once, at the start, with the whole list in front of you.

Ask before exporting
Every file it would replace, listed before the first render, with Skip or Overwrite on each row and Skip all / Overwrite all for the lot. The default.
A batch never stops halfway
Forty sequences and a name clash on the last one used to mean a dialog opening forty minutes in. Now the question comes at the click, so you can start it and walk away.
Ask during the export
The older behaviour, still here if you want it: one question per file, as it happens. It stops the export until you answer, so leave it off for anything you run unattended.
Or never ask
Always overwrite, or always skip and keep what is on disk. Only applies while the Overwrite switch on the main panel is off — with it on, files are always overwritten.

Off

No effect when rendering directly with Premiere Pro.
SETTINGSKeep finished renders
